_comment: Controller bases for the Build yours configurator. Every figure carries a basis: 'published' (quoted from the maker's page at 'source'), 'assumed' (not published; the reason is given) or 'not verified' (not found in the maker's documentation when this file was written). Lengths in mm, masses in g. Nothing here has been built or measured. Which locomotion each base supports, and through which drive, is said only in config/compat.json.

unoq_braccio.name: Arduino UNO Q with the Braccio shield and servos
unoq_braccio.status_reason: The six-servo biped on this base is the design this repository assembles digitally and simulates (reports/assembly.json, reports/sim.json): camera mount at the front of the deck, pin holes and studs on the parts. The simulation was run with the default camera preset; the other two presets were put through the digital assembly in short form. Nothing has been built.

mass_g.note: 30 g board plus 25 g shield, both estimates (config/hardware.json); the maker publishes neither. No battery: the robot is tethered.

mounting.value: Between two low rails on the torso deck, strapped through the deck slots with nonconductive ties, on 2.5 mm insulating spacers.
mounting.note: from the design README; spacer height assumed

actuates.value: Six hobby servos (four SR431, two SR311) through the Braccio shield.

channels.note: six servo outputs on the shield, one per kit servo

spare_pwm_pins.value: D2, D7, D8, D13, D20, D21 are reported free of the shield and PWM capable
spare_pwm_pins.note: read by another contributor from the Zephyr core overlay; not checked here

power.value: Board: USB-C 5 V up to 3 A, or VIN 7 to 24 V. Servos: the Braccio kit supply, regulated 5 V 4 A, through the shield.

cameras.esp32cam: Stands in the mount at the front of the torso deck; own torso file and fit piece in stl/. 5 V on its header pins; UART or Wi-Fi link, not written.
cameras.esp_eye: Own torso file and fit piece in stl/; checked in the digital assembly in short form. Powered and read through its Micro-USB socket.
cameras.esp32_s3_eye: Own torso file and fit piece in stl/; checked in the digital assembly in short form. Powered and read through its Micro-USB socket.
cameras.none: The mount is part of the torso and is left empty.
cameras.pixy2: Not possible on the biped: no torso is generated for it. Elsewhere on a UNO Q: Charmed Labs says an Arduino needs the general (non-LEGO) firmware; the Pixy2 Arduino library on the UNO Q is not verified, and the LEGO cable is not used.
cameras.picam2: Not possible: the Camera Module needs a CSI connector on a Raspberry Pi.

robot_creator.note: The Robot Creator profile schema has no family for an Arduino board.

unoq_braccio.software: app_lab/microduck_agent in this repository. Not built, not flashed.

pi_servo.name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W with a 16-channel servo driver
pi_servo.status_reason: The legs and servos are the analysed ones, but no deck, mount, wiring or software exists for a Raspberry Pi, and the analysis used the UNO Q stack's mass and position.
pi_servo.controller: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W (the model in the owner's LEGO prototype)

mass_g.note: the product page gives no mass. No battery assumed: tethered.

mounting.value: Four M2.5 holes on 58 x 23 mm centres.
mounting.note: figure from the owner's microduck-lego README; not checked against Raspberry Pi's mechanical drawing. The 40-pin header footprint is unpopulated (published): a header must be soldered.

actuates.value: Six hobby servos through an I2C PWM driver board (a PCA9685 16-channel board is the usual choice).
actuates.note: no specific driver board was checked against its maker's documentation

channels.note: channel count of a PCA9685 board; six used by the legs

power.value: Board: micro USB power, official supply recommended; the page states no current. Servos: a separate 5 V supply into the driver board, never the Pi's 5 V pin.

cameras.picam2: CSI-2 camera connector on the board (published); Zero-series ribbon.
cameras.esp32cam: UART or Wi-Fi; not written, not verified.
cameras.pixy2: USB to the Pi with Charmed Labs' software; not verified here. The LEGO cable is not used.

robot_creator.note: The Robot Creator profile schema has no Raspberry Pi family.

hub51515.name: LEGO MINDSTORMS Robot Inventor 51515 hub
hub51515.status_reason: No chassis has been drawn for this hub. The crank walker and wheeled variants are being analysed on another branch; their numbers are read from its summary file when it exists.
hub51515.controller: LEGO Technic Large Hub as sold in set 51515

outline_mm.note: LEGO Education's figures for the SPIKE Prime Large Hub 45601; that the 51515 hub has the same body is assumed

mass_g.note: without the battery (LEGO Education fact sheet, reseller-hosted copy). The mass of the rechargeable battery is not verified, so the working mass is not known.

mounting.value: Technic build geometry on the hub body (pin holes).

actuates.value: LEGO Powered Up (LPF2) motors and sensors. No hobby servo output is documented.

channels.note: six LPF2 input/output ports, A to F

power.value: The hub's own rechargeable battery, charged in the hub over micro USB. Current available per port is not verified.

cameras.pixy2: Not possible with the Pixy's LEGO cable: it is for NXT and EV3 sensor ports, and this hub's ports are LPF2. Charmed Labs documents Pixy2 for the EV3 only.
cameras.esp32cam: Not possible as a camera the hub can read: no connection to an LPF2 port is documented.
cameras.picam2: Not possible: needs a Raspberry Pi.

hub51515.software: Robot Creator generates beep, probe, drive and wave programs for these targets. No walking controller exists.

ev3.name: LEGO MINDSTORMS EV3 brick
ev3.status_reason: The owner's ev3-pixy2 prototype has printable parts and a geometric clearance check only: no fit test, no walking controller. It is being analysed on another branch; numbers are read from its summary file when it exists.

mass_g.note: no LEGO-published mass found. Runs on six AA cells or the LEGO rechargeable pack; either adds to the mass, by an amount not verified.

mounting.value: Strapped across the 130 x 116 mm deck of the prototype chassis through four slots.
mounting.note: from the owner's microduck-lego README and generator; not fit-tested

actuates.value: LEGO EV3 and NXT motors on four output ports, A to D. The Linux drivers list tacho-motor, dc-motor and led modes for the outputs; no hobby servo output.
actuates.note: ev3dev driver documentation, not a LEGO document

channels.note: four output ports and four input ports

power.value: Six AA cells or the LEGO rechargeable battery pack inside the brick. Motor stall current is not verified.

cameras.pixy2: Input port 1 to 4 through the Pixy LEGO cable. Charmed Labs: a regular Pixy2 works with that cable once Data out port is set to LEGO I2C in PixyMon; no firmware change is called for. Their EV3 block and Python class expose no servo control.
cameras.esp32cam: Not possible as a camera the brick can read: no connection to an EV3 port is documented.
cameras.picam2: Not possible: needs a Raspberry Pi.

ev3.software: Robot Creator generates beep, probe, drive and wave programs for these targets. No walking controller exists.

m5_basex_ev3.name: M5Stack Core with the BaseX base driving EV3 motors
m5_basex_ev3.status_reason: No chassis or mount has been drawn for an M5Stack Core on a BaseX, and Robot Creator has no code target for it. The motor-driven variants are being analysed on another branch.
m5_basex_ev3.controller: M5Stack Core (ESP32) stacked on the BaseX base

outline_mm.note: BaseX alone; the Core on top adds height by an amount not verified

mass_g.note: BaseX product weight, which the page lists with a built-in 950 mAh battery. The Core's mass depends on the model and is not verified.

mounting.note: no mounting holes or LEGO-compatible features are stated on the BaseX page

actuates.value: Four LEGO EV3 motors with angle and speed reading from 32-bit encoder registers, and two hobby servos. I2C address 0x22, STM32F030C8T6 on the base.

channels.note: four motor ports with encoders, two servo outputs, no LEGO sensor port

power.value: Motors: DC 9 to 12 V on a 3.5 x 1.35 mm jack, centre positive; the jack does not charge the battery. Built-in 950 mAh battery, charged through the Core's USB-C.

cameras.pixy2: The BaseX has no LEGO sensor port, so the LEGO cable is no use here. Pixy2 on the Core's I2C or UART with the general firmware: not verified.
cameras.esp32cam: UART or Wi-Fi to the Core: not written, not verified.
cameras.picam2: Not possible: needs a Raspberry Pi.

robot_creator.note: Robot Creator runs simulated probes for this family; its server refuses firmware generation: a code target is not implemented.

pi_buildhat_51515.name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W with the Build HAT driving 51515 motors
pi_buildhat_51515.status_reason: The owner's pi-zero-2w-51515 prototype has printable parts and a geometric clearance check only: no fit test, no walking controller. It is being analysed on another branch; numbers are read from its summary file when it exists.
pi_buildhat_51515.controller: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W under a Raspberry Pi Build HAT

outline_mm.note: the Pi Zero 2 W. The Build HAT is larger and overhangs it; its page gives the outline only as a drawing, so the HAT's size is not verified here.

mass_g.note: neither the Pi Zero 2 W page nor the Build HAT page gives a mass. No battery assumed: the 8 V supply is a mains adapter, so the robot is tethered.

mounting.value: Pi on four M2.5 posts at 58 x 23 mm centres on the prototype deck; the HAT above on 9 mm spacers (Raspberry Pi's figure) with a soldered 40-pin header.
mounting.note: post positions from the owner's generator; not fit-tested

actuates.value: LEGO Technic motors and sensors of the SPIKE portfolio and of the Robot Inventor kit, among them the 51515 Medium Angular Motor. EV3 and NXT devices are not mentioned.

power.value: One 8 V +/-10 percent supply able to give 48 W on a 5.5 x 2.1 mm centre-positive barrel jack powers the HAT, the Pi and the motors. Bookworm is required: Raspberry Pi says the HAT is not yet supported by Raspberry Pi OS Trixie.

cameras.picam2: CSI-2 connector on the Pi with the Zero-series ribbon, as in the owner's prototype. Ribbon clearance under the HAT is not stated by Raspberry Pi.
cameras.esp32cam: UART or Wi-Fi; not written, not verified.
cameras.pixy2: USB to the Pi with Charmed Labs' software; not verified here. The LEGO cable is not used.

robot_creator.note: The Robot Creator profile schema has no Raspberry Pi family. Raspberry Pi's python3-build-hat library drives the motors.

medium_angular_motor.name: LEGO Technic Medium Angular Motor (51515, 45603)
medium_angular_motor.note: LEGO Education fact sheet for 45603 (reseller-hosted copy); speed and current are +/-15 percent. Mass not on the sheet: not verified.

ev3_large_motor.name: LEGO EV3 Large Servo Motor (45502)
ev3_large_motor.note: Third-party pages give 20 N cm running and 40 N cm stall; not verified against a LEGO document. Stall current not verified.

ev3_medium_motor.name: LEGO EV3 Medium Servo Motor (45503)
ev3_medium_motor.note: Torque and current not verified against a LEGO document.

m5_servo_360.name: M5Stack 360 degree servo (Servo Kit 360; BALA-C)
m5_servo_360.note: Servo Kit 360 page: 'speed and direction controlled by adjusting the PWM duty cycle', so it turns continuously and holds no angle; LEGO-compatible mounting bracket. The BALA-C page lists two 9 g servos, rotation angle 360 degrees, 0.12 s per 60 degrees at 4.8 V, an L9110S driver and I2C address 0x38 in its base; it does not say the servos are the same part as the kit's, nor that they accept a PWM signal directly: not verified.

tt_motor.name: Yellow TT DC gear motor
tt_motor.note: A generic part with no single maker. Voltage, gear ratio, speed, torque and stall current are not verified. Without the encoder version, speed is open loop.

h_bridge.name: H-bridge driver board: TB6612FNG, DRV8833 or L298N
h_bridge.note: Pin names follow the chip makers' datasheets, which were not re-read for this file: TB6612FNG AIN1 AIN2 PWMA BIN1 BIN2 PWMB STBY; DRV8833 AIN1 AIN2 BIN1 BIN2 nSLEEP; L298N IN1 IN2 IN3 IN4 ENA ENB. Current ratings and voltage drop are not verified.

pixy2.name: Pixy2 (standard, non-LEGO) with the pan-tilt kit and the LEGO cable

published.input: USB 5 V or unregulated 6 to 10 V
published.outputs: UART serial, SPI, I2C, USB, digital, analog

pixy2.note: Which Pixy the owner has is not confirmed; Pixy2 is assumed. Pan-tilt kit mass and servo current are not published.

esp32cam.name: AI-Thinker ESP32-CAM
esp32cam.note: Dimensions, mass, supply and current are in config/hardware.json (cameras.esp32cam), from AI-Thinker's specification V1.0 read from a mirror: 40.5 x 27 x 4.5 mm, 10 g, 5 V, 180 mA with the flash LED off, 310 mA at maximum.

esp_eye.name: Espressif ESP-EYE
esp_eye.note: See config/hardware.json (cameras.esp_eye). Espressif publishes no dimensions or mass: 41 x 21 mm is a reseller's figure and 8 g an estimate.

esp32_s3_eye.name: Espressif ESP32-S3-EYE
esp32_s3_eye.note: See config/hardware.json (cameras.esp32_s3_eye). 60 x 30 mm from Espressif's board drawing; 25 g is an estimate.

picam2.name: Raspberry Pi Camera Module 2
picam2.note: Mounting holes 21 x 12.5 mm per the owner's generator; not checked against Raspberry Pi's drawing.

pixy_findings: The Pixy LEGO cable connects a Pixy2 to an NXT or EV3 sensor port (EV3 input ports 1 to 4). Source: Charmed Labs, Pixy2 EV3 block page.

A regular Pixy2 can be used with LEGO Mindstorms: it needs the Pixy2-to-LEGO cable and Data out port set to LEGO I2C in PixyMon's Interface tab. Charmed Labs does not call for a firmware change; Pixy2 for LEGO only ships with the LEGO firmware already loaded. PixyMon's About box says which firmware is on the camera, LEGO or general.
The Interface tab exists only under the stock (general) firmware. An Arduino needs the general firmware. Charmed Labs' Python class for the EV3 also asks for the stock firmware, I2C address 0x54.

Pan-tilt servos plug into the Pixy2's two RC servo connectors. The general API sets them with setServos(s0, s1), values 0 to 1000. The EV3 block (colour connected components, line tracking, RGB, signature compare, lamp) and the EV3 Python class have no servo call. Whether Pixy2's own pan-tilt demo runs while it answers an EV3 is not stated: not verified.
The 51515 hub's ports are LEGO Power Functions 2.0 (LPF2), a different connector from the NXT/EV3 port the cable fits. Charmed Labs documents no LPF2 connection.
joint_count_findings: The analysed biped has six position joints, one hobby servo each, and no head: its torso carries a fixed camera mount.
The EV3 brick has four output ports, the Build HAT four connectors, the BaseX four motor ports. The 51515 hub has six ports.

The owner's LEGO prototypes (microduck-lego) do not try to drive six joints. Each is a two-motor parallel-crank walker: one motor per side turns two cranks through three 16-tooth gears, and each leg hangs from the two crank tips. A third motor may pan the head; on four-port controllers one port is then spare.
So the LEGO-motor bases are a different mechanism from the six-servo biped, and are presented as such.
